'''Leopold Benno Felsen''' (May 7, 1924 – September 24, 2005) was a German-born American electrical engineer and physicist known for his fundamental contributions to [[electromagnetism]] and wave-based disciplines. For the most of his career, he was a professor of Electrical Engineering at Polytechnic Institute of Brooklyn, which later became [[New York University Tandon School of Engineering]].

== Biography ==
Leopold Benno Felsen was born on May 7, 1924, in [[Munich]]<ref name="ieee-memoriam">{{cite journal |last1=Stone |first1=W. Ross |title=In Memoriam: Leopold Benno Felsen (1924-2005) |journal=IEEE Antennas and Propagation Magazine |date=August 2005 |volume=47 |issue=4 |pages=151–152 |doi=10.1109/MAP.2005.1589915|bibcode=2005IAPM...47..151. }}</ref><ref name=LBF>{{cite journal | last=Felsen | first=L. B. | title=Radiation and Scattering of Transient Electromagnetic Fields | journal=International Journal of Numerical Modelling: Electronic Networks, Devices and Fields | volume=5 | issue=3 | date=1992 | issn=0894-3370 | doi=10.1002/jnm.1660050305 | pages=149–161 | url=https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/abs/10.1002/jnm.1660050305| url-access=subscription }}</ref> to Markus and Anna Felsen. He was of [[History of the Jews in Poland|Polish-Jewish descent]], with his father being a [[Second Polish Republic|Polish]] citizen. His family was persecuted by the [[Nazi Germany|Nazi regime]] due to their ancestry; in 1940, he was sent to the United States by his family to live with a relative. While his parents survived and joined him in the United States in 1946, many of his family members including his elder sister Johanna died during [[the Holocaust]].<ref name="ny-times">{{cite news | url=https://www.nytimes.com/2005/10/10/science/leopold-b-felsen-81-expert-on-the-properties-of-waves-dies.html | title=Leopold B. Felsen, 81, Expert on the Properties of Waves, Dies | newspaper=The New York Times | date=10 October 2005 | last1=Leary | first1=Warren E. }}</ref><ref name="erinnerungszeichen">{{cite web |last1=Hutzelmann |first1=Barbara |title=Johanna Felsen - Luisenstr. 7 |url=https://www.erinnerungszeichen.de/en/biografien/biografie/3205.0--Johanna-Felsen.html |website=erinnerungszeichen.de |access-date=January 25, 2023}}</ref>

He received his bachelor, master, and PhD degrees from the [[New York University Tandon School of Engineering|Polytechnic Institute of Brooklyn]], in 1948, 1950, and 1952, respectively, all in [[electrical engineering]].<ref name=LBF /> After his educations he became professor at [[New York University Tandon School of Engineering|Polytechnic Institute of Brooklyn]]<ref>{{cite web |url=http://engineering.nyu.edu/news/2006/05/04/felsen-family-endows-scholarship-poly |title=Felsen family endows scholarship at Poly |date=May 4, 2006 |website=[[NYU Polytechnic School of Engineering]]|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140529052831/http://engineering.nyu.edu/news/2006/05/04/felsen-family-endows-scholarship-poly |archive-date=2014-05-29 }}</ref> and at Boston University College of Engineering, an [[Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers|IEEE]] life fellow and a fellow of both the [[Acoustical Society of America]] and the [[Optical Society of America]].<ref name=LBF />

In 1973, he coauthored with his PhD advisor [[Nathan Marcuvitz]] a textbook titled ''Radiation and Scattering of Waves'' which published by [[Prentice Hall]] in its Electrical Engineering Series. This was a classic worldwide textbook which immediately became widely used by researchers<ref>{{cite book | last1=Felsen | first1=L. B. |author1-link=Leopold B. Felsen | last2=Marcuvitz | first2=N. | title=Radiation and Scattering of Waves | publisher=[[Wiley (publisher)|Wiley]]-[[Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers|IEEE]] | date=2003 | isbn=978-0-780-31088-9 | pages=vii-viii | url=https://www.wiley.com/en-us/Radiation+and+Scattering+of+Waves-p-9780780310889}}</ref> and has been described as "The Bible" in applied electromagnetism.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Leary |first1=W. E. |title=Leopold B. Felsen, 81, Expert on the Properties of Waves, Dies |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2005/10/10/science/leopold-b-felsen-81-expert-on-the-properties-of-waves-dies.html |website=[[The New York Times]] | date= October 2005 |access-date=January 31, 2024}}</ref> ''Radiation and Scattering of Waves'' was reissued by [[Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers|IEEE]] in 1994 and 2003 as one of classic reissues in the collection of ''The IEEE Press Series on Electromagnetic Wave Theory''.<ref>{{cite journal | last=Dudley | first=D. G. | title=The IEEE Series on Electromagnetic Wave Theory | journal=IEEE Antennas and Propagation Magazine | volume=48 | issue=6 | date=2006 | issn=1558-4143 | doi=10.1109/MAP.2006.323368 | pages=126–127 | bibcode=2006IAPM...48f.126D | s2cid=40484203 }}</ref>

Following his retirement from Polytechnic Institute of Brooklyn in 1994, Felsen relocated [[Boston]] to be near his family and accepted a faculty position at [[Boston University]], teaching there until his death. From 1970s onward, he lived with [[muscular dystrophy]]. He died on September 24, 2005, in [[Boston]], following complications from a surgery, and was survived by his two children and three grandchildren.<ref name="nytimes">{{cite web |last1=Leary |first1=W. E. |title=Leopold B. Felsen, 81, Expert on the Properties of Waves, Dies |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2005/10/10/science/leopold-b-felsen-81-expert-on-the-properties-of-waves-dies.html |website=[[The New York Times]] | date=2005 |access-date=23 December 2023}}</ref>

== Awards ==
In 1977, he was elected to the [[National Academy of Engineering]] "for his contributions to the theory and application of [[microwave]] [[Electromagnetic propagation|propagation]] in complex media and for leadership in engineering education."<ref name="NAE">[http://www.nae.edu/MembersSection/MemberDirectory/29397.aspx Dr. Leopold B. Felsen elected in 1977] as a member of [[National Academy of Engineering]] in [[List of members of the National Academy of Engineering (Electronics)|Electronics, Communication & Information Systems Engineering]] for his contributions to the theory and application of [[microwave]] [[Electromagnetic propagation|propagation]] in complex media and for leadership in engineering education.</ref> In 1991 he won the [[IEEE Heinrich Hertz Medal]].<ref>[https://web.archive.org/web/20120927170830/http://www.ieee.org/documents/hertz_rl.pdf Recipients of the IEEE Heinrich Hertz Medal],  [[Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers]].</ref><ref>[https://web.archive.org/web/20070515194510/http://www.ieee.org/portal/pages/about/awards/pr/hertzpr.html IEEE site]</ref>

===Authored===
*Felsen LB, [[Nathan Marcuvitz|Marcuvitz N]], ''Radiation and Scattering of Waves'', [[Wiley (publisher)|Wiley]]-[[Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers|IEEE]], 2003.

===Edited===

*Bertoni HL, Felsen LB, (Eds), ''Directions in Electromagnetic Wave Modeling'', [[Springer Science+Business Media|Springer]], 1991.
*Carin L, Felsen LB, (Eds), ''Ultra-Wideband, Short-Pulse Electromagnetics'', vol 2, [[Springer Science+Business Media|Springer]], 1995.
*Felsen LB, (Ed), ''Hybrid Formulation of Wave Propagation and Scattering'', [[Brill Publishers|Martinus Nijhoff]], 1984.
*Felsen LB, (Ed), ''Transient Electromagnetic Fields'', [[Springer Science+Business Media|Springer]], 1976.
*Pinto IM, Galdi V, Felsen LB, (Eds), ''Electromagnetics in a Complex World: Challenges and Perspectives'', [[Springer Science+Business Media|Springer]], 2004.

===Tributed===
*Russer P, [[Mauro Mongiardo|Mongiardo M]], (Eds), ''Fields, Networks, Computational Methods, and Systems in Modern Electrodynamics: A Tribute to Leopold B. Felsen'', [[Springer Science+Business Media|Springer]], 2004.
*Sevgi L, ''Electromagnetic Modeling and Simulation'', [[Wiley (publisher)|Wiley]]-[[Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers|IEEE]], 2014.
